To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the generalised scaling function for the third order is the same as the one for the second order and the generalised scaling for the fourth order is different from the one for the third order.

the third generalised scaling function does not receive any contribution from the non BES reducible operators and that the forth scaling function receives contributions from both the BES reducibles and non reducible operators.

the third and the fourth generalised scaling functions of the planar sl 2 N = 4 super-Yang-Mills theory have a strong coupling expansion which can be determined to high order, that they have different properties, and that they can be used as building blocks to determine all other generalised scaling functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the anomalous dimensions of the operators in N = 4 Super Yang-Mills theory.
the study of anomalous dimensions of composite operators in the planar N = 4 super Yang-Mills theory at strong coupling.
a new approach for the computation of the high spin behaviour in planar N = 4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory (SYM) and its string theory duals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the planar N = 4 sl ( 2, R ) sector of the theory, the O ( 4 ) NLSM is the correct effective field theory at the leading order in the large- n expansion.

the N = 4 planar SYM anomalous dimension of the Konishi operator is the only one that can be described by the O ( 4 ) NLSM mass-gap, and that the NLSM mass gap is the unique one that is related to the anomalous dimension of a single operator.
the O ( 4 ) NLSM mass-gap is the first and only one emerging from the SYM ‘mass functions’ and, therefore, is a universal feature of the planar theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the O ( 4 ) sigma model mass-gap is the only one to emerge from a non-BES reducidble contribution, while the others come only from the BES reducible part of the SYM anomalous dimension.
the generalised scaling function is a powerful tool to understand the emergence of the sigma model mass-gap and its relation to SYM ‘masses’.
the NLSM mass-gap is not a ‘mass’ but an ‘interaction’.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generalised scaling function f n ( g n ), for n > 4, are all non-trivial functions of g n, with f 4 ( 1 ) = 2, f 5 ( 1 ) > 2, and f 6 ( 1 ) ≈ 2.5.
the generalised scaling function f 4 ( x 2 ), which is the first function to show the emergence of the non-BES contributions, is the one that also exhibits the first interaction in the NLSM.

the generalised scaling function f n ( g ), n ≥ 3, can be computed at strong coupling and that it is crucial for disentangle the emergence of the mass-gap in the O ( 4 ) NLSM from different SYM mass functions.
